window: Covering reporting published since the Sept 16 edition, roughly Sept 15-17, with a few incident dates running back to Sept 10-11 where reporting lagged. The dominant federal story today is not a seizure but a policy document: the White House's annual presidential drug-certification determination for fiscal year 2027, announced Sept 16, which removed Venezuela from the list of countries judged to have 'failed demonstrably' on counternarcotics while keeping Colombia and Bolivia on it. No new SOUTHCOM/JTF-WHEM lethal strike or vessel interdiction was confirmed since the refueling-vessel takedown already logged in the Sept 16 edition; a Sept 17 aggregator item citing '68 strikes' and an August death toll appears to recycle stale figures inconsistent with the 69-strikes/230-deaths count already logged Sept 10, so it was excluded. A Pinellas County, Florida cocaine-ring press conference and a Colombia 1,918 kg marijuana highway seizure both surfaced in searches but were dropped as stale, dating to July 14 and Sept 13 respectively and, in the Colombia case, overlapping with hauls already logged Sept 13. A Wilmington, Delaware fentanyl case was dropped after search results returned contradictory dates and quantities for what appears to be the same underlying arrest, and a Timmins, Ontario raid was excluded for lacking any reportable drug-quantity detail. A DEA-announced Ecuador cocaine interdiction (3,284 kg) was also dropped because the agency's own post did not specify a date or location, making it too underdetermined to write confidently.
